thread:
Emily (cs): FYI customer ticket #2345 — they saw a flood of 503s from Hosted API starting ~20:10 UTC. Partial streaming responses, some got cut off. Auth succeeded, but requests timed out and returned 503. Can we triage?
Ravi (sre): Alert shows upstream pool had ~12 runner exits in 5m, kube restarted pods. Events: OOMKilled and then Sigsegv on some pods. @Alex can you grab runner logs + GPU usage?
Alex (eng): grabbing logs now, pasting top snippets below:
```
[2026-03-17T20:10:12Z] runtime: fatal error: segfault
#0  0x7fffdc1a in runtime.kv_prefetch_slice+0x42
#1  0x7fffdc2b in infer.runtime:kv_prefetch_loop
[stack trace omitted]
[2026-03-17T20:10:13Z] CUDA error: out of memory (cuMemAlloc)
[2026-03-17T20:10:13Z] process 12345 (python) killed: SIGSEGV
```
Alex (eng): nvidia-smi snapshot at same time:
```
GPU 0  78.2GiB / 78.2GiB (100%)  processes: python(pid=12345)
GPU 1  2.1GiB / 78.2GiB
```
Jordan (support): Customer says this happened when they sent a very long context + toolcall (streaming). They included an auth header; no auth failures. Could this be a client-side retry flood?
Ravi (sre): I'm not seeing a sudden ramp of QPS to that tenant, traffic looks typical. But the requests were large (context sizes ~400k bytes) which matches KV prefetch heavy paths.
Alex (eng): initial hypothesis: KV-prefetch window ballooned on long-context streaming, triggering a mem balloon then CUDA OOM and subsequent segfault in the prefetch path. I couldn't find a recent quant swap around 20:10.
Alex (eng): quick repro attempt locally with a long prompt (reduced):
```bash
curl -sS -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" -d '{\"model\":\"rwd-large\",\"input\":'\$(printf 'x%.0s' {1..50000})'\"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
Alex (eng): when I ran a stress with context ~50k tokens on a canary runner, memory climbed and I hit cuMemAlloc failure then process crash.
Emily (cs): Customer asked whether we can route them to Dedicated while we investigate. Any fast mitigations?
Ravi (sre): Short-term mitigations: 1) enable model-variant fallback to smaller instance (if available) for affected tenants, 2) throttle extremely long contexts at gateway for hosted, 3) bump restart backoff to avoid thundering restarts.
Alex (eng): Pushed a quick change to limit prefetch window to 8GB and enable kv-eviction on canary. Also added extra nullptr checks in prefetch loop to avoid segfault on partial allocation failure. Rolling to canary now.
oncall-bot: Deploy started -> canary group=canary-13 image=runner-hotfix-prefetch-20260317-1
Alex (eng): Canary has been up ~15m, no segfaults and CUDA allocations stayed <75% on the canary GPUs. Monitoring running.
Jordan (support): CS to customer: we rolled a hotfix to canary and will roll to affected pools if stable. Suggested temporary workaround: pin to a model variant with smaller KV memory use or use Dedicated.
Emily (cs): I'll relay that. Please log a follow-up issue with repro steps, telemetry to capture context length and prefetch bytes on future crashes. Also add a regression test with long streaming payloads.
Alex (eng): noted. Created GH issue rwd/infra#4789 with repro steps and telemetry checklist. Also scheduled a load test that hits max context sizes.
Ravi (sre): Postmortem action items: 1) add kv-prefetch soft caps and clear metrics, 2) add socket-level backpressure to avoid request queueing into prefetch-heavy code path, 3) tune OOMKill handling to emit more diagnostics before restart.
Emily (cs): Thanks all. CS updated customer with mitigation and ETA for a broader roll. Will reopen if we see recurrence. :white_check_mark:
